about.title: Irwindale Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Irwindale is a small city, but its stretch of the I-605 and I-210 interchange carries heavy commuter and freight traffic every day, and Arrow Highway adds local cross-traffic into the mix. Public records show 162 injury collisions and 229 injured people in the most recent final year, with crashes clustering on Friday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. — a pattern likely tied to weekend traffic building on the freeways. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the moments after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness contact information can disappear quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that matches injured people with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Our goal is simply to help you get to the right person sooner, so you're not figuring out California's claim process alone while you're trying to heal.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing With the Insurer

items.title: California Gives You Only Two Years
items.desc: Most car accident injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims involving a government entity — like a city road issue — can require notice in as little as six months. Missing that window can end your case before it starts.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but the insurer will try to shift blame onto you to reduce what they pay. An attorney can push back on unfair fault allocations before they become the final word.

items.title: There's No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. That makes it especially important not to accept a quick lowball offer before the full extent of your injuries is known.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally not a good idea to give a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to find ways to reduce or deny your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened at the I-605 and I-210 interchange?
items.answer: That interchange sees significant traffic volume, and multi-vehicle collisions there can involve more than one insurance company or driver. An attorney can help sort out liability between multiple parties and make sure evidence from the scene is preserved before it's lost.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: LawProactive's connection service is free, and independent attorneys in the network typically work on contingency. That means there's no fee unless you receive a settlement or award.
